verdicts.flaw_description: A live confounder that reaches every unit: "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle, and every machine here drew from that supply." A higher-grade synthetic lubricant is itself a known cause of longer bearing life, so the 260-410 extra hours cannot be attributed to the redesigned bearing.

The measured population is narrower than the claim: "Rates cover the patients discharged from each ward" while "each ward transferred out a quarter of those admitted" - so roughly 25 percent of admissions, plausibly the sickest and most infection-prone, are excluded from the infection rate entirely.

A competing cause applies to all four cohorts: "The free trial ran thirty days, four times its length in the earlier period, and every cohort here signed up on that trial." Quadrupling the trial length directly inflates week-two retention, so the 3-6 point lift is not attributable to the onboarding email.

Two of the four cohorts have outcome dates preceding enrolment: cohort One "started 4 April; by 29 March" and cohort Three "started 5 October; by 30 September" - the measured heart-rate drop is dated before the app was started, so those cases cannot show any effect of it.
